source: User attribution on 2026-09-03 from preserved r22 logs plus read-only checkout timestamps; timestamps below are user-supplied, not new harness observations.
historicalResult: failed readiness; not reclassified as a pass
attribution: Attribution from the preserved r22 evidence plus read-only file timestamps in the Fireside checkout on the host: the Fireside stack launched at about 12:49:00. All four log markers were satisfied by 12:49:21: Next "Ready in 522ms" at about 12:49:05, "All emulators ready" at about 12:49:17 (the mprocs UP transition, between the images and cache-watcher anchors), cache watcher started at 12:49:18, .NET "Now listening" at 12:49:21 after a 5-second incremental build. The unmet condition was the frontend login probe. The Fireside checkout had never compiled /login/[loginType]: apps/templates/.next/dev/build was created at 12:49:29 and build-manifest.json was written at 12:50:05, so the Turbopack cold compile took about 40 seconds, and the first completed request then took 14.7 seconds of cold SSR, logged at 12:50:19. Every earlier probe was cut off by curl --max-time 8 while that compile ran, and the deadline expired at about 12:50:00. The official checkout is warm, its .next/dev is 2.4 GB from seven prior boots, and its first login response in r22 was 7.7 seconds, within 0.3 seconds of the 8-second cap. This is checkout warmth and probe budget, not a Fireside defect: Fireside's own readiness marker came 17 seconds after launch. Do not rerun blindly. The Fireside checkout is now warm, so an unchanged r23 would probably pass for the wrong reason.
